
# Appendix C: R5 Spacecraft 10 (R5-S10) Flight Results


## Purpose
This file captures basic context and information on the flight performance of the star tracker algorithm onboard R5-S10.

As of November 2026, this is the most complete known flight data set of this algorithm.  It's important to note that several
substantial bug fixes have since been applied, but have not yet been flown, so this performance may not be indicative of the 
expected performance of the latest state of the code base.  This data set is presented primarily for completeness and as lessons
learned.

## Context
R5-S10 ran the v1.2 version of the COTS Star Tracker software (approximately commit d01d9b1) using a single Ximea MC023 camera
with a Fujinon HF35HA lens as the imager.

R5-S10 was deployed into LEO and was tumbling after its brief proximity operations flight phase at the start of its mission and
the rotation rate is captured.  This was the first flight of v1.2, which included errors codes.  The telemetry system on R5-S10
was configured to downlink the most recent star tracker solution and discarded the rest.

The R5-S10 mission is still operating and this data is through November 23, 2026.  Additional analysis will be completed and
released after the end of mission, expected in 2027.

Publications:
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20260005643
* https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20260008063

## Lessons Learned
The mission is still in progress and lessons learned are still being gathered.

## Flight Data
As stated above, the R5-S10 mission is still operating and this data is through November 23, 2026.  Additional analysis will be 
completed and released after the end of mission, expected in 2027.

### Brief Analysis
R5-S10 has gathered images over at least 763000 seconds across 122 operational periods.  In this time, it has attempted 531484
star tracker solves and successfully completed 20451, for a solve rate of 3.85%.

Of the 531484 solution attempts, 1023 were downlinked via telemetry.  These solutions were downlinked as they were the most
recent before the assembly and transmission of the telemetry packet and are therefore a random sample across the mission duration
thus far.

Of the 1023 downlinked, 26 appear to be valid quaternions, 617 report error code 400, 365 report error code 408, and 2 report
error code 402.  There are no other error code outputs in this data set. The remaining downlinked solutions are invalid (all 0s),
suggesting the star tracker app was not operating during that time period.

Of the 617 reporting error code 400 (insufficient number of centroids), 578 had an average pixel value of 255 (max value), 
suggesting those images were completely blown out.  All of these outputs had 0 centroids found.

### Data Description
* timestamp_s is the unix time in seconds associated with the time_met_s
* time_MET_s is the Mission Elapsed Time in seconds at which point the data was downlinked
* time_BET_s is the Boot Elapsed Time in seconds at which point the data was downlinked
* st_st_img_id is the image ID of the image associated with the downlinked star tracker solve data
* st_st_num_attempts is the number of attempts at star tracker solves (each image only gets 1 attempt, if any)
* st_st_num_solves is the number of successful solves
* st_quat_scalar, st_quat_0, st_quat_1, st_quat_2 are the quaternion constituents
* camxic_image_count is the number of images taken by the star tracker camera, which wraps at TBD
* camxic_temp_deg_c is the temperature readout from the star tracker camera in degrees Celsius
* cpu_percent is the percentage of the flight computer CPU being used
* ram_percent is the percentage of the flight computer RAM being used
* disk_percent is the percentage of the flight computer nonvolatile storage being used
* num_boots is the number of the current spacecraft boot (also called operational period)
* imu_imu_temp_deg_c is the temperature readout from the IMU in degrees Celsius
* imu_w_body_filt_rads describe each axis of the sensor body angular rate in radians per second
* imu_w_body_filt_degs describe each axis of the sensoy body angular rate in degrees per second
